source.quote: Beneficial ownership of the Corporation’s Class A and Class B Stock on March 5, 2025 ... Percentage of Aggregate Voting Power of Class A and Class B ... Percentage of Aggregate Economic Interest of Class A and Class B ... Warren E. Buffett Class A 206,359 37.9 Class B 951 * 30.4(2) 14.4

structure.note: Two classes. Each Class A share has one vote and each Class B share 1/10,000 of a vote; Class B has 1/1,500 of the dividend and distribution rights of Class A, and each Class A share converts into 1,500 Class B shares. On March 5, 2025 there were 544,953 Class A and 1,339,905,639 Class B shares outstanding. The proxy says Buffett 'may be deemed to be Berkshire’s controlling shareholder', but his 30.4% of the vote is below 50%, and a voting agreement makes him vote any shares above 49.9% of total voting power proportionately with other shareholders, so controlled is false under this schema's >50% test.

notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 (matches data.js fy 'Dec 2024'). Sources: FY2024 Form 10-K (accession 0000950170-25-025210) and 2025 proxy statement (DEF 14A, accession 0001193125-25-054877), both read on EDGAR. LEADER: the proxy table states Buffett's percentage of aggregate economic interest of Class A and Class B (14.4%) and of aggregate voting power (30.4%) as of March 5, 2025, so no derivation was needed. The governance section of the same proxy rounds these to 'approximately 30.3% of the voting interest and 14.3% of the economic interest'; the table figures are used. His Class A count includes 360 shares held by a private foundation in which he disclaims beneficial interest. Relation is 'chair' (Chairman and CEO since 1970; director and controlling shareholder since 1965). Howard G. Buffett and Susan A. Buffett (his children, both directors) hold 0.1% or less of economic interest each; they are not added as a family figure because the proxy gives no family aggregate. HOLDERS left empty: the proxy gives the other large holders only as a percentage of one class (FMR 6.1% of Class A; Vanguard 11.1%, BlackRock 8.2% and State Street 5.3% of Class B, all from Form 13F reports for the quarter ended December 31, 2024). It does not give their share of total economic interest, and converting class percentages would be a derivation, so they are omitted. STOCK COMP: null. The FY2024 10-K has no share-based compensation expense line or note, and the proxy states the policy quoted above, but no company-wide expense figure (including any at subsidiaries) is disclosed, so 0 is not asserted. GEOGRAPHY: null. The 10-K does not report total revenue by geography; the only geographic split is insurance premiums written by region (based on the domicile of the insured), which covers one business, not total revenue.
